claims.text: The initial HEA has a relatively coarse or stress-introduced microstructure.
The initial HEA has an equilibrium passive film formed under static conditions.
Sliding-induced shear can produce an ultra-nanocrystalline or dynamically amorphized near-surface layer in an HEA.
The shear-induced near-surface layer promotes formation of a stable, self-healing passive film.
The shear-induced surface state governs the coupled tribo-corrosion response.
The shear-induced surface state simultaneously limits wear loss and reduces local corrosion rates.
Shear-induced dynamic recrystallization or amorphization creates an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
Shear-induced surface refinement enriches or reconfigures the passive film.
Surface microstructural refinement alters local chemical reactivity and enables rapid in situ formation or repair of a corrosion-resistant passive film.
An ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer is associated with lower friction and improved wear resistance.
Total tribo-corrosion degradation will be less than the simple sum of isolated wear and corrosion losses.
The wear component may be modestly increased relative to the stated baseline because of mechanical action.
The corrosion rate will be significantly reduced by enhanced passivation from the nanocrystalline layer.
The prediction should hold for alloys capable of shear-induced nanocrystallization and development of a self-healing passive layer.
The prediction may fail when the alloy forms an unstable, spalling oxide scale that does not benefit from shear-induced modification.
